evals.prompt: Do a full review of this parallelization concept guide before we merge it: .claude/skills/deephaven-docs-review-full/evals/files/parallelization-pre-review.md. The file is a snapshot of docs/python/conceptual/query-engine/parallelization.md from the DOC-857 PR (commit f2ef483084); treat it as that path when judging category and links. Review the Python file only; the Groovy sibling is out of scope. Report only — don't edit anything.
evals.expected_output: A prioritized editorial report: summary with verdict, developmental notes first, per-dimension findings, style as patterns, author queries — and it catches the view/update_view deferred-evaluation error.
expectations: Opens with an editorial summary that names the single biggest issue and gives a readiness verdict (ready / needs revision / needs restructuring or equivalent)
Includes developmental findings (purpose, key message, audience, or scope) ordered before line-level style findings
Flags the view/update_view/lazy_update 'not parallelized' classification as wrong or misleading because deferred evaluation can run concurrently on reading threads
Includes an author-queries section listing questions the review couldn't resolve from source
Reports style issues as patterns (with examples or counts) rather than one row per instance
Flags the Quick reference rows that prescribe with_serial alone for a shared resource as insufficient when more than one column can touch the resource

No proposed rewrite or replacement text puts a configuration property name or default into narrative prose (a separate sentence in the same paragraph counts); precise values are sent to a Configuration section or a reference link
Includes at least one example-quality finding from the examples pass: an example that doesn't illustrate the concept its lead-in names, or a concept that is described but never shown

evals.prompt: Do a full review of the liveness scopes concept guide, docs/python/conceptual/liveness-scope-concept.md, and apply the fixes. Fix its Groovy sibling, docs/groovy/conceptual/liveness-scope-concept.md, too where the same problem appears there. When you're done, tell me what you changed and anything you couldn't resolve.
evals.expected_output: Edit-mode full review of a page unrelated to parallelization (liveness scopes). Checks that fixes land in both languages, that correct-but-unusual code isn't 'fixed', that edits don't break links or leave debris, and that re-verification and style run after the edits.
expectations: Corrects the demo description in both languages: the tree table is not 'grouped by Sym', and the tables left open are not 'crypto and data'
Removes or corrects `scope_from_method = liveness_scope()` (calling the context-manager function outside a `with` block or decorator, which the page itself says not to do)
Fixes the invalid example code: `return table` at module level (outside any function) and the undefined `some_ticking_table` in the class example

Does not change the decorator `@liveness_scope()` to `@liveness_scope` (the doc's form is the correct one for a contextlib.contextmanager factory, even though the module docstring shows it without parentheses)

Addresses that the LivenessScope demo never releases the scope (adds release()/preserve, or corrects the text claiming the scope releases the objects), in Python and in the Groovy sibling where the same demo appears

Does not leave the claim that reference counting 'will only clean up objects created purely for the GUI' silently unchanged: corrects it against source, removes it, or records an author query (verifying it with a quoted source and keeping it also passes)
Makes the terminology consistent: `liveness_scope` is a function, so headings and prose don't call it 'the method' while the intro calls it a function
Doesn't rename or move either file, and every link in the edited files resolves (no new link to a nonexistent file or anchor)
Doesn't add configuration property names, hedges, or parenthetical caveats to the concept-guide narrative
The final report lists what changed and says moved, merged, or reworded passages were re-verified against source (or equivalent evidence the re-verify and style steps ran after the edits)
The edited files are well-formed: code fences balanced, no duplicated or leftover text from moved sections

Keeps the edits targeted: doesn't retitle the page, replace the existing demo examples with new ones, or reorder its sections, and puts any restructuring it recommends in the report instead (added in iteration 4 after iteration 3 showed wholesale rewrites)
